# Race-detector shards of the CI `race` job (`go test -race`), read by
# race-shard.py. Under a "[N]" header, one entry per line:
#
#   ./pkg                 the package's tests
#   ./pkg -run <regexp>   the package's tests that <regexp> selects
#   ./pkg -skip <regexp>  all the others: a package split in two lists both
#                         halves, with the same regexp, in two shards
#   *                     every package of `go list ./...` no line names
#
# A shard starts its packages in the order written, so the slowest come
# first (a slow package started late is what bounds a shard); the packages
# "*" takes follow in `go list` order. A package named twice (other than the
# two halves of a split), a split whose halves differ, a package that does
# not exist or an empty shard fails the job.
#
# Balance by CPU time, not by wall time: on a 4-vCPU runner the race shards
# are CPU-bound (CI run 38305819365: about 1.8 to 2 cores' worth of CPU per
# second of a shard, the lower for the busier shards), so a shard takes about
# max(its slowest package's wall time, its packages' CPU time / 1.8). The
# comments are each package's race run alone with GOMAXPROCS=4, warm build
# cache: wall time / CPU time (user + sys), in seconds — measured for v6.5.0
# on a developer machine (Xeon W-2140B, macOS), about 1.1 to 1.5 times the
# 4-vCPU runner's time; what matters is their proportion. Changing the
# shards changes what each shard compiles: bump its line in cache-keys/ too.
[1]
./internal/tsparse                    # 142 / 342
[2]
./internal/resolver                   # 111 / 365
[3]
./internal/languages/golang           # 103 / 255
./internal/languages/typescript       #  50 /  47
./tests/integration                   #  66 /  72 (with the cache build tests: scaled from a re-measure, this machine 40/41 → 59/74)
[4]
./internal/completion                 #  63 /  14 (mostly waiting)
./internal/golden                     #  61 /  60
./internal/secrets                    #  52 /  60
./internal/mcp                        #  36 /  46
./internal/languages/rust             #  21 /  15
./internal/languages/html             #  18 /  17
./internal/languages/php              #  15 /  15
*                                     # the rest: about 90 CPU seconds
